brief.greeting: Good morning. While LLMs are busy reading X‑rays, Google is busy telling phone makers to lock down their phones.

stories.headline: LLM cross‑checks X‑ray reports with images
stories.body: **Quick sanity check:** Rad‑Linter fine‑tunes a 1.5 B‑parameter model on 1,816 examples and scores 98.5% agreement when matching reports to image‑derived pathology scores.
stories.why: It shows language models can audit radiology notes without extra data pipelines.

stories.headline: Hybrid LLMs get transparent cache layer
stories.body: **Cache‑aware serving:** TideCache runs on CPU‑GPU superchips, automatically juggling heterogeneous caches and streaming layers so GPUs stay busy only when needed.
stories.why: Reduces GPU memory pressure, letting you host larger models on the same hardware.

stories.headline: Google pressures OEMs to block GrapheneOS
stories.body: **Policy push:** Google is urging device makers to discourage GrapheneOS installs and to stop offering bootloader unlocks, tightening control over custom ROMs.
stories.why: Limits developers’ ability to run hardened OSes, affecting security research and custom firmware work.

quick_hits.text: **Performance:** OpenAI’s Performance Factory auto‑fixes regressions to keep ChatGPT snappy.
**Model size:** SmolVLM2‑256M‑Video‑Instruct packs 256 M parameters and already has 45 k downloads.
**Security:** Thursday updates hit AlmaLinux, Debian, Fedora, Mageia, Slackware, and SUSE.
**Framework:** Tenon unifies PIM compilation across heterogeneous memory‑centric accelerators.

highlights.title: Multimodal Error Detection in Chest X-ray Reports: A Large Language Model Reading Image Evidence
highlights.summary: Rad-Linter uses a 1.5B-parameter language model fine‑tuned on 1,816 examples to compare chest X‑ray reports with image‑derived pathology scores, achieving 98.5% pair accuracy on a controlled 131‑quad evaluation.
highlights.detail: The system pairs each report with score vectors from other patients to create consistent and inconsistent pairs, ensuring that any single input yields only 50% chance of correct classification. It outperforms a keyword‑and‑negation rule baseline, which reaches 80.5% accuracy under the same conditions.

highlights.title: TideCache: Efficient Hybrid LLM Serving with Transparent Cache Management and Layer-Wise Streaming
highlights.summary: TideCache is a serving system for hybrid LLMs on CPU‑GPU superchips that transparently manages heterogeneous caches and streams layer‑wise data to reduce GPU residency.
highlights.detail: It introduces a Transparent Cache Pool that reallocates physical pages while keeping virtual addresses stable, and a Cache Streamer that prefetches global‑attention prefixes during bounded‑state layer intervals, overlapping transfers with computation. The Request Scheduler decides between resident and streamed cache usage based on workload.

highlights.title: A CPU Inside an LLM: Zero-Gradient Compilation of Exact Circuits into Pretrained Weights
highlights.summary: The authors present a zero‑gradient method that compiles exact arithmetic circuits directly into pretrained LLM weights without any training data, preserving natural‑language ability.
highlights.detail: The technique leverages Mellin‑GLU quadrature over bias‑free SwiGLU/GeGLU layers to map RMSNorm scaling onto a log‑spaced gate grid, and uses Chebyshev‑based self‑sink attention with SiLU‑antisymmetric shifts to cancel cross‑token scaling. It provides IEEE‑754 error bounds while keeping the model’s original competencies intact.

items.title: How OpenAI’s Performance Factory keeps ChatGPT fast
items.summary: OpenAI’s Performance Factory is a Codex‑driven workflow system that automatically discovers and fixes performance regressions to keep ChatGPT responsive.
items.detail: The factory continuously profiles the service, generates patches for identified bottlenecks, and validates improvements before deployment. By integrating code generation and testing, it reduces manual tuning effort and helps maintain low latency as the model and infrastructure evolve.

items.title: Model: HuggingFaceTB/SmolVLM2-256M-Video-Instruct
items.summary: SmolVLM2‑256M‑Video‑Instruct is a 256‑million‑parameter image‑text‑to‑text model on Hugging Face with over 45k downloads and 286 likes.
items.detail: The model is designed for video instruction tasks, supporting multimodal inputs and generating textual responses. Its popularity reflects community interest in lightweight video‑capable vision‑language models.

items.title: Model: apple/FastFrames-L
items.summary: apple/FastFrames‑L is a text‑to‑video model on Hugging Face that has received 366 community likes.
items.detail: FastFrames‑L focuses on generating short video clips from textual prompts, leveraging Apple's research on efficient video synthesis. The model is publicly available for experimentation and integration.

items.title: Model: briaai/RMBG-3.0
items.summary: The briaai/RMBG-3.0 model for image‑segmentation on Hugging Face has been downloaded 103 times and received 164 likes.
items.detail: It provides background‑removal capabilities for images and is listed among trending models, indicating community interest despite modest download numbers.

items.title: Google is pushing OEMs against GrapheneOS and bootloader unlocking
items.summary: Google is pressuring OEMs to discourage the use of GrapheneOS and to block bootloader unlocking.
items.detail: The move is being discussed on Hacker News, reflecting concerns that the policy could limit user‑controlled devices and affect the security‑focused Android ecosystem.

items.title: Security updates for Thursday
items.summary: Thursday’s security updates were issued for AlmaLinux, Debian, Fedora, Mageia, Slackware, and SUSE, covering dozens of packages.
items.detail: Updates include components such as nginx, OpenJDK 21/25, Firefox, and the Linux kernel, aiming to patch known vulnerabilities across the major distributions.

items.title: [$] Added indirection allows for larger BPF programs
items.summary: A new indirection feature in the BPF verifier reduces the exponential state‑space growth caused by complex control flow.
items.detail: Patch author Alexei Starovoitov reworks state tracking, improving verification performance for large BPF programs while preserving existing safety guarantees.

items.title: Four PHP security releases including fixes for critical vulnerabilities
items.summary: PHP released security updates 8.5.13, 8.4.28, 8.3.37, and 8.2.36, fixing critical remote‑code‑execution bugs that require non‑default configurations.
items.detail: The pre‑release announcement on November 18 notes that the critical flaws are exploitable only in uncommon setups, and Linux vendors are expected to push updated packages soon.

items.title: PHP 8.6.0 released
items.summary: PHP 8.6.0 was released, adding a polling API, clamp() function, SortDirection enum, and a Time\Duration class.
items.detail: The new features aim to simplify asynchronous I/O, numeric clamping, sorting direction handling, and duration manipulation, expanding the language’s standard library.

items.title: PostgreSQL 19 released
items.summary: PostgreSQL 19 has been released, adding a REPACK (CONCURRENTLY) command for non‑disruptive table optimization, a pg_plan_advice extension for plan stability, and various performance improvements.
items.detail: The new REPACK command lets administrators reorganize tables while they remain online, reducing downtime for maintenance. pg_plan_advice provides actionable hints to keep query plans stable across schema changes. The release also includes broader performance tweaks, though the full list is in the official release notes.

items.detail: LLM agents run long, multi-turn programs whose contexts grow at every step, and serving them is limited by KV cache capacity. items.title: Matching Architecture to Workload: Comparing RISC-V Parallel Accelerators for Energy-Efficient Embedded Computing
items.summary: A comparative study of three open-source RISC‑V accelerators—PULP Cluster (scalar multicore), Snitch Cluster (streaming multicore), and Spatz (vector processing)—implemented in the same 12 nm process shows no single model dominates all workload classes.
items.detail: The evaluation uses a common benchmark suite to measure energy efficiency across diverse embedded workloads. Spatz excels on regular, highly vectorizable tasks, while the other two perform better on irregular or scalar‑heavy kernels. The results guide architects in selecting execution models based on workload characteristics.

items.title: awslabs/cli-agent-orchestrator
items.summary: aws‑labs/cli‑agent‑orchestrator is a Python tool that runs multiple AI coding agents like Claude Code, Kiro, and Codex in isolated tmux sessions for coordinated execution.
items.detail: The orchestrator launches each agent in its own tmux pane, allowing parallel interaction and easy switching. It abstracts the underlying CLI differences, enabling users to experiment with several models without manual session management.

items.title: wshobson/agents
items.summary: wshobson/agents provides a Markdown‑based framework to define plugins, agents, skills, and commands for various AI coding tools, then generates validated adapters for each target.
items.detail: Authors write a single specification in Markdown, and generators produce compatible code for Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor, OpenCode, Antigravity CLI, GitHub Copilot, and Pi. Validation and evaluation steps ensure the generated adapters meet each tool's requirements.

items.title: intrinsic-ai/intrinsic-core
items.summary: intrinsic‑ai/intrinsic‑core offers an open, hardware‑agnostic runtime and SDK for real‑time control of industrial robots, running locally without cloud dependencies.
items.detail: The framework abstracts robot hardware details, providing a unified API for motion planning and sensor integration. Its local execution model reduces latency and improves safety for time‑critical automation tasks.

items.title: microsoft/markitdown
items.summary: microsoft/markitdown is a Python utility that converts various file formats and Office documents into Markdown.
items.detail: It supports batch processing and preserves basic formatting such as headings, tables, and lists. The tool simplifies migration of legacy documentation to Markdown‑friendly platforms like GitHub or static site generators.

items.title: 0xPlaygrounds/rig
items.summary: 0xPlaygrounds/rig is a Rust library for building modular, scalable LLM applications.
items.detail: The crate provides composable components for prompt management, response handling, and integration with multiple language model providers. Its design emphasizes type safety and performance for production‑grade AI services.

items.title: FlashML-org/FreeVideo
items.summary: FreeVideo is an open‑source Python tool that generates videos using the MiniMax H3 model, requiring as little as 8 GB VRAM and 16 GB system RAM.
items.detail: The software automatically selects the optimal acceleration path based on the host hardware, allowing it to run on consumer‑grade machines without specialized GPUs. It is hosted on GitHub and currently trending among Python repositories.
